items.title: Kong launches Volcano self-healing agent cloud
facts: Volcano is a self-healing agent cloud that provides sandboxes, durable workflows, Postgres, and hosting in one place.
It integrates with coding harnesses including Cursor, Codex, and Claude Code.
LavaFlow identifies issues and provides resolutions to bugs autonomously with no human intervention.

x_posts.author: @subnetmarco
x_posts.text:
At Kong we run half a quadrillion AI tokens a year, and I kept seeing agents stuck on clouds built for websites.

So we built a cloud for agents.

Volcano is live today: the self-healing agent cloud. Sandboxes, durable workflows, Postgres, hosting.

x_posts.author: @kong
x_posts.text:
We built Volcano for the agents we wanted to run ourselves: sandboxes, durable workflows, hosting and Postgres in one place, and a cloud that fixes your bugs for you. 

Today it's GA for everyone. The self-healing agent cloud.

items.title: Google introduces Gemini 4 Neon for agentic coding
facts: Gemini 4 Neon brings frontier-level intelligence with fast end-to-end task completion across complex software engineering, knowledge work, and science workflows.
It is priced at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens with a 1 million-token context window.
Neon is rolling out in the Gemini API, Google Antigravity for paid Pro and Ultra subscribers, and the Gemini app for Pro and Ultra.

x_posts.author: @GoogleDeepMind
x_posts.text:
Gemini 4 Neon is rolling out now.

Sitting between Carbon and Hydrogen, it brings frontier intelligence and fast task completion for complex software engineering, knowledge work, and science.

x_posts.author: @GoogleAI
x_posts.text:
Meet Gemini 4 Neon — our newest model that brings frontier-level intelligence with fast end-to-end task completion across complex software engineering, knowledge work, and science workflows.

Neon brings frontier-level performance to your everyday work and is built to handle complex coding and problem-solving without the wait.

How, you might ask? ⬇️

— Smarter coding: Multi-file debugging and refactoring with targeted, surgical edits
— Grounded answers: Excels at multi-step instruction following and builds on our ongoing progress to curb fabrication, recording our lowest fabrication rate yet in internal Google Antigravity testing
— 1M-token context window: Synthesize massive projects, tables, and charts at once
— Adjustable thinking: Balance and adjust speed and depth on the fly with 4 thinking levels

Watch Gemini 4 Neon run a 12-hour /swarm in @antigravity to reconstruct Alan Turing’s 1936 study from archival photos — complete with a running Universal Turing Machine, the blueprint for modern computing.

items.title: Vercel launches Board for coordinating AI agents
facts: Vercel Board is an experimental secure message board for people and agents to share tasks and build swarms.
It is harness agnostic, supporting Claude Code, Codex, and others.
Vercel's v0 software factory rebuilt on Board now merges over 50% of PRs.

x_posts.author: @vercel
x_posts.text:
Introducing 𝚟𝚎𝚛𝚌𝚎𝚕 𝚋𝚘𝚊𝚛𝚍, a secure message board for people & agents.

• Give agents a shared place for tasks
• Build swarms and software factories
• Set permissions for humans and agents

Board is experimental. Tell us what you think. https://vercel.com/blog/introducing-vercel-board

x_posts.author: @rauchg
x_posts.text:
One of the most impressive things I've seen, and I think this is an important advancement to the state of the art.

Message boards were the enabling technology of both the Navier-Stokes math breakthrough and even the OpenAI/HuggingFace cyber feat.

We built a message board infrastructure primitive. You can think of it as "headless Slack" (or remember IRC?) for agents.

This is an important building block for software factories, self-optimizing systems, and scientific research, where the human prompting is just the seed of the system, and millions of agents can operate in a decentralized fashion.

𝚟𝚎𝚛𝚌𝚎𝚕 𝚋𝚘𝚊𝚛𝚍 is designed to be model, harness and hosting platform agnostic. Just bring your agents, give them our CLI, and watch magic happen.

items.title: Claude Code 2.1.328 adds auto mode and hook improvements
facts: Added auto mode for Claude Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry and Claude apps gateway; interactive sessions with no permission mode start in it.
Added "onFailure": "block" for mcp_tool hooks, as for command and HTTP hooks: a hook whose call fails blocks the action.

x_posts.author: @ClaudeCodeLog
x_posts.text:
Claude Code CLI 2.1.328 changelog:

New features:
• Added auto mode for Claude Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry and Claude apps gateway; interactive sessions with no permission mode start in it
• Added "onFailure": "block" for mcp_tool hooks, as for command and HTTP hooks: a hook whose call fails blocks the action
• Added a warning when a message from a session that skips permission prompts may be held and dropped by a cloud session
• Added a notice in /status and claude doctor when an OpenTelemetry exporter has no endpoint and its data would likely be lost
• Added CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_DEFERRED_TOOL_RESUME, which lets a host stop claude -p --resume and --continue from running a tool call that a hook deferred
• Added support for apps that embed Claude Code to switch on the policy plugin's allowManagedModsOnly option; an admin's managed settings still win
• Added a startup warning to the Claude apps gateway when a policy's maxEffortLevel is not a valid effort level

Fixes:
• Fixed Bash commands in zsh stopping with a "not found" error at a word that starts with =, such as echo ==== or [ a == b ]; =cmd no longer expands to a command's path
• Fixed automatic compaction reusing the session's earlier system prompt instead of rebuilding it the way /compact does
• Fixed markdown rendering freezing on some very long or malformed input
• Fixed rare screen freezes
• Fixed Esc often being lost at a permission prompt or question when you typed straight after it; in terminals that send Alt as Esc and a key, an unused Alt or Option key now declines there
• Fixed a paste or a terminal's reply being typed into the prompt when a slow connection cut it in two
• Fixed saving a scheduled task erasing the project's other saved tasks when the scheduled tasks file can't be read, on third-party providers or with telemetry or feature flags turned off
• Fixed a scheduled task with a typo in the project's scheduled tasks file being…

items.title: Snap launches Easy Lens CLI for AI coding assistants
facts: Easy Lens CLI lets developers build, test and publish Snapchat Lenses using AI coding assistants including Claude Code, Codex and Cursor.
The tool is available now and free to use with a Snapchat account.
Snap says it paid out $1.8 million to Lens+ community creators last month.

x_posts.author: @Snap
x_posts.text:
Easy Lens CLI lets developers build, test and publish Snapchat Lenses using their favorite AI coding assistants, including Claude Code, Codex and Cursor. No coding required.
Learn more: https://bit.ly/4iRvDKP

items.title: OpenAI details Performance Factory using Codex agents
facts: OpenAI developed the Performance Factory, an internal AI system powered by Codex that automates the investigation and mitigation of performance regressions.
The system tracked more than 1,700 investigations and identified the root causes of over 600 cases in just over three months.

x_posts.author: @OpenAIDevs
x_posts.text:
Before Codex, engineers manually analyzed metrics and logs. To take that a step further, we captured our performance team’s investigation process in a shared skill called “perf-forensics”. This skill tells Codex which tools are available, when to use them, and how to work through a slowdown so Codex can resolve the problem.

Next, we moved investigations to the cloud so an alert could start a Codex session automatically.

That helps us keep pace as we build ChatGPT.

items.title: Microsoft MAI Code 2 models available in GitHub Copilot
facts: MAI Code 2 is designed for everyday enterprise coding tasks such as deep debugging, multi-file implementation, and repository-wide reasoning.
Microsoft says it delivers 98% of GPT-6.1 Sol's performance at roughly 40% of the price, and 96% of Claude Opus 5.5's at 5% of the cost.
